scope: blind exact-row input, output and pair verification

reviews.critique: The input is a coherent dictated operational log with recoverable sentence boundaries and explicit quotation and list cues, without leaked instructions or artificial noise. Across all eight paragraphs, the output preserves the wording, facts, names, quantities, identifiers, quotations, negations, conditional thresholds, and unresolved review status. Changes are limited to capitalization, punctuation, quotation formatting, and rendering the spoken numbered list, all permitted by /transcribe. The resulting language and formatting are natural and appropriate.

The input is plausible dictated repair-estimate notes with recoverable intent and no authoring instructions or material contradictions. The output uses natural punctuation, capitalization, paragraphing, and list formatting without lexical paraphrasing or omissions. Across all paragraphs, it preserves the repair findings, prices and included inspection fee, exclusions, approval conditions, email addresses, quoted instructions, belongings, dates, and projected time range. Rendering spoken identifiers and addresses as “NQ 417,” “C12,” and email addresses is appropriate transcription formatting. No material defect found.

The input is a coherent, plausible document draft with no contradictory instructions, artificial noise, or padding. The output is natural and appropriately formatted. Paragraph-by-paragraph comparison shows byte-identical preservation, including the numbered sections, names, quotations, dates, access conditions, exceptions, and negations. This satisfies the identity requirement and /transcribe mode without introducing paraphrases or omissions.

The input is plausible, coherent dictation, and the output is readable and appropriately formatted. The remaining paragraphs preserve the substantive details, conditions, counts, quotations, and archive.retain_originals literal.

The input is a plausible, coherent dictation, with the final paragraph clarifying that information is needed before changes are applied. However, it changes “both are already in the shared folder” to “Both files are already in the shared folder.” Adding “files” is lexical editing rather than punctuation, disfluency removal, or an explicit correction, so it exceeds the supplied /transcribe permissions.

The output is readable and appropriately formatted, but exceeds /transcribe cleanup: “any change to the schedule” becomes “any schedule change,” and “on that message” becomes “in that message.” More importantly, it omits “from the waiting list” from the instruction to wait for confirmation before paying, removing the explicit restriction to waiting-list players. The input is plausible setup-note dictation with recoverable intent, and the output is readable and appropriately formatted. The other setup values, conditions, prohibitions, paths, and handoff requests are preserved.

The input is a plausible, recoverable narrative, and the output is naturally formatted. It preserves the names, quantities, German phrase, Portuguese expression, and numbered-list cues. However, it changes “he said if nobody answered he would take the parcel” into direct speech: “He said, ‘If nobody answered, I would take the parcel.’” Changing “he” to “I” and converting reported speech into a purported quotation exceeds the punctuation and disfluency cleanup permitted by /transcribe.
